name: Kuramei Sprint 5 — Simulador + Histórico + Onboarding + Cancel Lembrete
description: De 1 usuário (Alexandre) para 10-20 usuários reais de Fase 0. Critério: Alexandre convida 5 amigos, eles mandam mensagem, o produto responde com contexto de conversas anteriores, conseguem criar e cancelar lembretes. Alexandre consegue testar qualquer fluxo localmente sem usar WhatsApp.

userStories.title: WhatsApp Simulator + @kuramei/agent-core (extração do agent-processor)

AgentCoreConfig type: { openRouterApiKey: string, dynamoDbTable: string, remindersTable: string, cloudflareAccountId: string, cloudflareKvNamespaceId: string, cloudflareApiToken: string, kurameiJwtSecret: string, kurameiBaseUrl: string }

processMessage contains ALL logic currently in apps/agent-processor/src/index.ts: LLM call (OpenRouter/DeepSeek), ToolRegistry setup, ExperiencePackages loading, buildSystemPrompt, tool execution, response handling
Load all 4 ExperiencePackages inside processMessage: navigationExperience, reminderExperience, weatherExperience, currencyExperience

Simulator UI: mensagens do agente — bubble esquerda, fundo branco, texto escuro

Simulator UI: typing indicator (três pontos animados) enquanto aguarda resposta

userStories.notes: CRITICAL ARCH: agent-processor becomes a thin Lambda wrapper. All business logic moves to @kuramei/agent-core. simulator-api is another thin wrapper (Express). Both call the same processMessage function — guarantees production parity. Do NOT duplicate logic between Lambda and simulator. The simulator is a dev tool only — never deployed.

userStories.title: Histórico de conversa — DynamoDB sliding window 20 msgs, TTL 30 dias
userStories.description: O agente precisa lembrar do contexto da conversa atual. Sem isso, parece amnésico — cada mensagem é respondida como se fosse a primeira.
acceptanceCriteria: Create (or verify/update) table kuramei-conversations in infra/cdk/lib/dynamo-stack.ts: PAY_PER_REQUEST, PK=PK (String), SK=SK (String), TTL attribute name: 'ttl'
Add CONVERSATIONS_TABLE env var to .env.example and .env.production.example
In packages/agent-core/src/process-message.ts, before calling the LLM:
- Load conversation history from DynamoDB: query PK='CONV#{userId}', SK begins_with 'MSG#', Limit=20, ScanIndexForward=false (newest first), then reverse result to get chronological order
- Each DynamoDB item: PK: 'CONV#{userId}', SK: 'MSG#{ISO_timestamp}#{uuid}', role: 'user' | 'assistant', content: string, ttl: Math.floor(Date.now()/1000) + (30*24*60*60)
Inject history in LLM messages array: [...history.map(h => ({ role: h.role, content: h.content })), { role: 'user', content: currentMessage }]
After receiving LLM response, persist 2 items in DynamoDB (user message + assistant response) with TTL = now + 30 days. Use timestamp+uuid for SK to ensure uniqueness.
Add CONVERSATIONS_TABLE to AgentCoreConfig type in packages/agent-core/src/process-message.ts
Update apps/agent-processor/src/index.ts to pass CONVERSATIONS_TABLE from process.env to AgentCoreConfig
Update apps/simulator-api/src/index.ts to pass CONVERSATIONS_TABLE from process.env to AgentCoreConfig (use 'kuramei-conversations' as default for dev)
pnpm build passes
pnpm typecheck passes
userStories.notes: The @kuramei/conversation package (ported from dikta) may already have DynamoDBSessionManager — check if it can be used or if it needs adaptation. If it needs major changes, implement directly in agent-core to avoid breaking existing package. Goal: inject up to 20 messages (10 exchanges) as context before current message. TTL is a DynamoDB epoch seconds number (not ISO string).

userStories.title: Onboarding de novos usuários — boas-vindas + coleta de nome
userStories.description: Quando um número novo manda a primeira mensagem, o Kuramei apresenta-se, coleta o nome e dá boas-vindas. A partir daí, usa o nome do usuário nas respostas.
acceptanceCriteria: Create (or verify/update) table kuramei-users in infra/cdk/lib/dynamo-stack.ts: PAY_PER_REQUEST, PK=PK (String), SK='PROFILE' (hardcoded in code)
User item schema in DynamoDB: PK: 'USER#{userId}', SK: 'PROFILE', name: string | null, registeredAt: ISO string, status: 'onboarding' | 'active'
Add USERS_TABLE env var to .env.example and .env.production.example
In packages/agent-core/src/process-message.ts, at the start of processMessage (BEFORE LLM call):
1. Load or create user from kuramei-users table using getOrCreateUser(userId, usersTable): checks if item exists; if not, creates with status='onboarding', name=null, registeredAt=now

2. If user.status === 'onboarding' AND user.name === null: return immediately with hardcoded response 'Olá! 👋 Sou o Kuramei, seu assistente pessoal via WhatsApp. Como posso te chamar?' — do NOT call LLM

3. If user.status === 'onboarding' AND user.name === null AND this is NOT first ever message: check if previous message was the welcome prompt by checking DynamoDB conversation history (last assistant message contains 'Como posso te chamar'). If yes: treat currentMessage as the user's name. Trim whitespace, capitalize first letter. Update DynamoDB: name=trimmedName, status='active'. Return 'Oi, {name}! Fico feliz em te conhecer 😊 Posso te ajudar com lembretes, navegação, clima, cotação de moeda, e muito mais. O que você precisa?'

4. If user.status === 'active': continue to LLM call with name injected in system prompt: append to base system prompt: 'O nome do usuário é {user.name}. Use o nome dele(a) nas respostas quando natural.'
Add USERS_TABLE to AgentCoreConfig type
Update apps/agent-processor/src/index.ts to pass USERS_TABLE from process.env
Update apps/simulator-api/src/index.ts to pass USERS_TABLE (default 'kuramei-users' for dev)
Onboarding flow MUST be hardcoded/deterministic — do NOT pass to LLM. Reason: guarantee consistent onboarding experience.
pnpm build passes
pnpm typecheck passes
userStories.notes: The onboarding name detection logic: after welcome message is sent, next user message IS the name. Use conversation history (loaded in US-002) to detect this: if last assistant message contains 'Como posso te chamar', current message = name. Store name trimmed + first letter capitalized. Whitelist: NOT needed in Sprint 5 — Fase 0 is private by number obscurity.

userStories.title: Cancelar lembrete — cancel_reminder tool + UX de desambiguação
userStories.description: Completar o lifecycle de lembretes. Usuários vão inevitavelmente querer cancelar — sem isso o product experience está incompleto.
acceptanceCriteria: Add tool cancel_reminder to packages/experiences/reminder/src/index.ts
cancel_reminder Zod input schema: { reminderId: z.string().min(1) }
cancel_reminder handler: update DynamoDB item PK='USER#{userId}', SK='REMINDER#{reminderId}' — set status='cancelled', add cancelledAt=new Date().toISOString(). Use UpdateExpression.
On success: call generateUI() with MessageSpec: { type: 'message', title: 'Lembrete cancelado ✅', body: '{reminder.text} — removido', actions: [] }

On not found (item doesn't exist or status already != 'pending'): call generateUI() with MessageSpec: { type: 'message', title: 'Lembrete não encontrado', body: 'Não encontrei esse lembrete. Use a lista de lembretes para ver os pendentes.', actions: [] }

cancel_reminder tool description: 'Cancels a pending reminder by ID. Use when the user wants to delete, remove, or cancel a specific reminder. IMPORTANT: requires the exact reminder ID — call list_reminders first if you do not have the ID yet. If the user refers to a reminder by description (e.g. "the medication reminder"), use list_reminders to find the matching ID before cancelling.'

Update reminderExperience.systemPromptSection to include cancel contract: 'Ao cancelar lembrete: se não souber o ID exato, chamar list_reminders primeiro para obter os IDs. Se houver múltiplos lembretes que podem corresponder à descrição do usuário, mostrar a lista e pedir confirmação antes de cancelar. Nunca cancelar sem ter o ID correto.'
Update reminderExperience.tools to include cancel_reminder alongside create_reminder and list_reminders
pnpm build passes
pnpm typecheck passes
userStories.notes: UX flow: (1) user says 'cancel medication reminder' → agent calls list_reminders internally → if exactly one matches: cancel directly with inline confirmation → if 2+ match: generate ListSpec with candidates + ask user to confirm → user picks → agent uses conversation history (US-002) to resolve reference → cancels. The disambiguation logic is in the LLM (via tool description + system prompt contract) — not hardcoded in the tool handler.

keyDecisions: US-001: @kuramei/agent-core extracts ALL business logic from agent-processor; Lambda and simulator-api become thin wrappers
US-002: conversation history sliding window of 20 messages (10 exchanges), TTL 30 days DynamoDB epoch
US-003: onboarding is hardcoded/deterministic — never delegated to LLM
US-003: no whitelist in Sprint 5 — Fase 0 private by number obscurity
US-004: disambiguation logic lives in LLM (via tool descriptions + systemPromptSection), not in handler
Simulator is dev tool only — never deployed, userId fixed 'simulator-dev'
